classification.difficultyReason: Compare candidates by the relationships between their markings, distinguishing a hypotenuse from a leg and an included angle from a non-included angle. Then select the valid congruence test and translate the matching vertices into the correct order.

content.prompt: In each part, name the triangle congruent to $\triangle ABC$. State the congruence test used.

spec.description: Reference triangle ABC, with horizontal AB, one tick on AC, alpha at A and beta at C. Decorative blue source strokes become ordinary black.
spec.mathematics: AC has one equality tick; angle BAC is alpha; angle ACB is beta.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens visible; no answer annotations.

spec.description: Candidate DEF with horizontal DE, one tick on EF, alpha at D and beta at E; ordinary strokes black.
spec.mathematics: EF has one equality tick; angle EDF is alpha; angle DEF is beta.

spec.description: Candidate GHI with one tick on HI, alpha at H and beta at I; ordinary strokes black.
spec.mathematics: HI has one equality tick; angle GHI is alpha; angle HIG is beta.

spec.description: Candidate JKL with one tick on JL, beta at J and alpha at K; ordinary strokes black.
spec.mathematics: JL has one equality tick; angle KJL is beta; angle JKL is alpha.

answer.worked: $\angle BAC=\angle GHI=\alpha$, $\angle ACB=\angle HIG=\beta$, and $AC=HI$ (marked). Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle HGI$ by AAS, with $A\leftrightarrow H$, $B\leftrightarrow G$ and $C\leftrightarrow I$.

spec.description: Reference ABC with A above CB; one tick on AC, two on AB and three on CB; ordinary strokes black.
spec.mathematics: AC, AB and CB belong to the one-, two- and three-tick classes respectively.

spec.description: Candidate STU retains the source's one tick on SU and three ticks on each of ST and UT; ordinary strokes black.
spec.mathematics: SU has one tick; ST and UT each have three ticks. The repeated three-tick class is intentional source content.

spec.description: Candidate XYZ retains two ticks on each of XY and YZ and three on XZ; ordinary strokes black.
spec.mathematics: XY and YZ each have two ticks; XZ has three ticks.

spec.description: Candidate RPQ with one tick on RP, two on RQ and three on PQ; ordinary strokes black.
spec.mathematics: RP, RQ and PQ match AC, AB and CB respectively.

answer.worked: $AB=RQ$, $BC=QP$ and $AC=RP$ (matching side marks). Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle RQP$ by SSS, with $A\leftrightarrow R$, $B\leftrightarrow Q$ and $C\leftrightarrow P$.

spec.description: Four separate triangles in source order ABC, LMN, SUT and VXW. Retains every vertex, right-angle square and side-mark class. Ordinary source blue strokes become black.
spec.mathematics: ABC: right angle B, AC one tick, BC two. LMN: right angle L, MN one tick, LN two. SUT: right angle U, SU one tick, UT two. VXW: right angle X, XW one tick, VX two.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens only; no candidate is identified as the answer.

answer.worked: $\angle ABC=\angle MLN=90^\circ$. The hypotenuses satisfy $AC=MN$ (one tick), and $BC=LN$ (two ticks). Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle MLN$ by RHS.

spec.description: Four separate triangles in source order ABC, DMN, LVS and XYZ. Preserves the position of each marked angle relative to the marked sides. Ordinary strokes black.
spec.mathematics: ABC: AB two ticks, AC one, included angle A alpha. DMN: DM one, MN two, angle D alpha. LVS: LS two, VS one, angle V alpha. XYZ: XY two, YZ one, included angle Y alpha.

answer.worked: $AB=YX$ (two ticks), $AC=YZ$ (one tick), and $\angle BAC=\angle XYZ=\alpha$. These are the included angles between the matching sides. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle YXZ$ by SAS.
